attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the warning in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization fairly captures a firm conditional warning, retaining the safety-improvement antecedent and absence of a deadline.

contract.note: Including recoverable operational harm is an ordinary reading of accident. The contract appropriately requires separate evidence of the antecedent, whose threshold and industry-wide versus deployment-specific scope remain unspecified.

evidence.note: Timely reporting supports the post-publication deployment-accident component. It does not establish the absence of radical safety improvement.

The operator's disclosure corroborates deletion and recovery and describes safeguards. It supplies relevant condition context, but neither independently establishes the antecedent nor refutes an accident merely because recovery succeeded.

reviews.rationale: The packet establishes a consequential agent-driven deletion, despite eventual recovery. It does not establish whether the stipulated absence of radical safety improvement held. The early-resolution rule therefore is not met, and an open-ended conditional forecast cannot be scored from this incident alone.
